# P2: Sleep diaries or wristbands?

Citation: Quill, R., & Danso, M. (2018). Methods in Sleep Studies, 5(1), 20-33.
Type: methods paper (n = 310 students)

Abstract: Students kept a sleep diary for two weeks while also wearing a wristband that records movement. Diaries over-reported sleep by about 40 minutes a night. The authors advise using wristbands for any study that depends on exact sleep length.

My notes: Useful for judging how far to trust the other studies' sleep figures.
